summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of recurrent epigastric abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting was admitted for acute on chronic pain management. She presented with two weeks of worsening pain, inability to tolerate oral intake, and intermittent diarrhea. Initial labs showed a mildly elevated lipase, but normal liver and kidney function, and no signs of infection. Imaging was not performed, and prior studies including MRCP and ERCP were consistently normal. A recent HIDA scan showed a gallbladder ejection fraction of 55%, not low enough to indicate biliary dyskinesia, and a specialist review did not recommend cholecystectomy. She was kept NPO initially, given IV fluids, and treated with IV pain and anti-nausea medications. Her diet was advanced to clear liquids, then soft, and finally regular diet as symptoms improved. Pain and nausea were controlled with oral medications. Her psychiatric medications were continued, and she remained stable mentally. She was discharged home with PRN hydromorphone and prochlorperazine, instructions to follow up with her gastroenterologist, and a plan to manage future flare-ups conservatively.
